newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Cotton prices seen steady in Pakistan, up in India.
newsitem.headline: Cotton prices seen steady in Pakistan, up in India.

text.p: Cotton prices are likely to stay steady to weak next week in Pakistan amid uncertainty about the size of the crop, while in India prices may firm on tighter availability, dealers said on Thursday.
Dealers in Karachi said prices rose this week on fears of a shortfall in the 1996/97 (July-June) crop, despite official estimates saying output would exceed nine million 375-lb bales.
An official committee said on Sunday the crop would reach 9.2 million to 9.5 million bales, down from a target of 10 million bales and the 1995/96 crop of 9.96 million bales.
But dealers said heavy demand from nervous spinners and low supply from ginners kept prices up for most of the week.

However, on Thursday, prices eased on a report by the private Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association, which said cotton output had reached 3.31 million bales by November 1, well up on the 2.04 million bales harvested by the same date last year.
In the kerb market NIAB-78 traded at 2,300 rupees ($57.19) per maund, K-68 at 2,300 and MNH-93 at 2,290, dealers said.
Following are the KCA's weekly cotton prices in rupees per maund ($1 = 40.22 rupees)-
Thursday Wednesday Oct 31
Indian traders said cotton prices were expected to remain firm in the next few days as India prepares to celebrate Diwali, the festival of lights, which falls on Sunday.
"Market activity will be dull until Diwali and for a few days after that," said a trader.
On the Bombay market, prices firmed after opening subdued this week as pre-Diwali arrivals dwindled, traders said.
"Prices at the start of the week were dull because of higher new crop arrivals but later on looked up on eased supplies," said one trader.

In spot, Bengal-deshi rose 50/70 rupees to 920/960 rupees per maund (37.32 kg). Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) initially dropped 900/1,000 rupees to 18,500/19,500 rupees but rose to 19,000/20,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
"Prices in the later part of the week turned firm also on reports that the government may allow more export of cotton," one broker said.
The government has so far authorised exports of 500,000 bales in the 1996/97 season (Oct-Sept). It allowed 1.59 million bales for export in 1995/96.
The state-run Cotton Advisory Board (CAB) meets in Bombay on November 21 to assess demand and supply in the current season.
Traders said they expected the government to take a decision on further exports based on the CAB assessment.
Traders have estimated India's 1996/97 cotton crop at 16 million bales, about the same as in the previous year, and believe there is room for exporting as much cotton as in 1995/96.
Textiles minister R. L. Jalappa said on Thursday that 1996/97 output was expected to reach a record 18 million bales against 15.6 million in the previous year.
